question: In the CTT individual-participant meta-analysis, what did statin therapy do to cancer incidence across ages?

options.A: It increased cancer at every age
options.B: It had no effect at any age on cancer incidence or cancer death
options.C: It prevented all cancers over age 75
options.D: It increased cancer only under age 65

correctAnswerText: It had no effect at any age on cancer incidence or cancer death
explanation: The authors report no effect at any age on non-vascular mortality, cancer death, or cancer incidence [1].
sourceArticle: Efficacy and safety of statin therapy in older people: a meta-analysis of individual participant data from 28 randomised controlled trials

question: What proportional reduction in major vascular events was seen per 1.0 mmol/L lower LDL cholesterol?
explanation: Overall, statin therapy or a more intensive regimen produced a 21% proportional reduction in major vascular events per 1.0 mmol/L LDL reduction (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.77–0.81) [1].
sourceArticle: Efficacy and safety of statin therapy in older people: a meta-analysis of individual participant data from 28 randomised controlled trials

question: How many participants were older than 75 at randomisation?
explanation: 14,483 (8%) of 186,854 participants in the 28 trials were older than 75. Median follow-up was 4.9 years [1].
sourceArticle: Efficacy and safety of statin therapy in older people: a meta-analysis of individual participant data from 28 randomised controlled trials

question: Where do the authors say direct evidence of benefit is more limited?

options.B: Patients older than 75 without known occlusive vascular disease
options.C: Anyone with a prior myocardial infarction

correctAnswerText: Patients older than 75 without known occlusive vascular disease
explanation: The interpretation states there is less direct evidence of benefit among patients older than 75 who do not already have occlusive vascular disease [1].
sourceArticle: Efficacy and safety of statin therapy in older people: a meta-analysis of individual participant data from 28 randomised controlled trials

question: Which safety statement is supported by this meta-analysis?

options.A: Statins raise non-vascular mortality after age 75
options.B: There was no adverse effect on cancer or non-vascular mortality in any age group
options.C: Statins cause cancer in 10% of older adults
options.D: Myopathy occurred in half of participants over 75

correctAnswerText: There was no adverse effect on cancer or non-vascular mortality in any age group
explanation: Despite previous concerns, the collaboration found no adverse effects on cancer or non-vascular mortality in any age group [1].
sourceArticle: Efficacy and safety of statin therapy in older people: a meta-analysis of individual participant data from 28 randomised controlled trials
